clue.text: Two things a lineman must be able to do with hoisting equipment.

definitions.text: Two things a lineman must be able to do
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an American football lineman has to ... opponents ... the ball carrier
second meaning: a set of pulleys and rope used to lift heavy loads

explanation.walkthrough: A lineman also suggests a telephone worker up a pole with lifting gear, but here he is a football player whose two jobs name the gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Blocking and tackling are the core duties of a gridiron lineman, and the same phrase names a pulley rig for lifting.

clue.text: Something special given at the wharves, or other really out-of-the-way locations.

parts.note: a boon is a welcome gift or favour
docks are wharves where ships tie up

explanation.surface: A special delivery made at the docks, or somewhere even more remote.
explanation.definitionFit: The boondocks is an American idiom for remote backcountry, far from towns.

clue.text: It's the very best sort of pot, with one little flower.

indicators.note: a sort of pot is the same letters arranged into a different kind of word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral one
mum is a short, familiar name for the chrysanthemum

explanation.surface: Praise for a prize flowerpot holding a single small bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns POT into OPT; mum is short for chrysanthemum, the 'little flower'.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the best possible, the most favourable degree or amount.

clue.text: See 22
See 1
Dramatizes Cats, possibly, but not in the end.

indicators.note: the end says this piece is placed last in the answer
possibly says the letters of Cats might form another word

parts.note: taken as written
out is the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A note on staging the musical Cats, except for its finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CATS into ACTS; 'not in' gives OUT, put at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To act something out is to perform it as a scene, the plain sense of dramatize.

clue.text: Led the wrong way around what Boreas is responsible for, to gradually disappear.

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters wrap round the other piece
the wrong way says the letters of Led are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written
Boreas is the Greek god of the north wind

explanation.surface: Someone misled by the north wind, fading away as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' scrambles the first word into DLE, and 'around' splits that round the north wind's product.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to shrink steadily until little or nothing is left.

clue.text: For example, Gore ends up thus, too.

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US vice-president, is a man called Al
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: Al Gore ends up this way as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and too are synonyms, both adding an item to what was said.

clue.text: I'd get a lousy mark when the ruler is about to be making a joke of things.

indicators.note: is about says the ruler wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a king is a ruler
taken as written, without the apostrophe
D is a poor grade on a school report

explanation.surface: A pupil gets a bad grade as the king prepares to laugh it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts the ruler around I'D plus D; D is a near-failing grade in American schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidding means joking or teasing, not being serious.

clue.text: Not a late Civil War general, certainly!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: arriving before the expected time, the opposite of late
second meaning: Jubal ..., a Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' could mean dead, but the clue wants its opposite, and the general's surname is that opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Early is the antonym of late, and it was also the surname of Confederate commander Jubal Early.

clue.text: The mail that's not in your in-basket, possibly–where the recipient is far away.

definitions.text: where the recipient is far away

parts.note: letters not in the in-tray are in the out-tray
post is another word for mail

explanation.surface: An office scene: the outgoing letters are bound for someone stationed far off.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement or military station, far from the centre.

clue.text: Such trading might not be approved of, being not out on the team, right?

definitions.text: Such trading might not be approved of

parts.note: in is the opposite of out; a batter not out is in
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A sports pundit doubts a trade involving a player still on the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Insider trading uses confidential company information to deal in shares, and it is illegal.

clue.text: The wrong mode for the top of the building, possibly.

definitions.text: the top of the building, possibly

indicators.note: the wrong mode is the word with its letters in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect complains the roofline was designed in the wrong style.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a rounded roof that can crown a building.

clue.text: Sold a variety of heavy things to cart around.

indicators.note: a variety of these letters is another arrangement of them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shop sold all kinds of bulky goods for hauling.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads are burdens or cargoes that have to be carried.

clue.text: Was Tim so like the woodman to your beginning?

parts.note: the Tin Woodman is the character in The Wizard of Oz

indicators.note: beginning says only the opening letter of your is used

parts.note: first letter Y

explanation.surface: A question asking whether Tim resembled the Tin Woodman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' takes just the opening letter of 'your'. Tiny Tim is the sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's character is called Tiny Tim, so small is what Tim was.

clue.text: A slinky type, but a little firm with support for some ladies.

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A sly character, but a small lingerie company makes him respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobra is a snake, and slinky describes its sinuous movement.

clue.text: Find a winning portion once more.

parts.note: a gain is what is won or profited

explanation.surface: An instruction to look for one's share of the winnings for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means one more time, a repeat of what has happened before.

clue.text: Make your debut, when the answer is not a way to get in.

indicators.note: is not says the answer reverses the sense of the invitation, swapping in for its opposite

parts.note: come in is the phrase that invites someone inside

explanation.surface: Advice for a debutante: the right response is not a way inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come in' lets you enter; 'is not' swaps IN for its opposite, OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out is to make one's first formal appearance in society, as a debutante does.

clue.text: Throws into gear, possibly, with a wise-crack perhaps seen to occur about it.

indicators.note: about says the shuffled letters go round the joke
perhaps says the letters of seen may be read in another order

parts.note: taken as written
a gag is a joke or wisecrack

explanation.surface: Someone shifts a car into gear while a joke is overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SEEN into ENES, which goes 'about' GAG as EN...ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage a gear is to put the mechanism into it, so throwing into gear is engaging.

clue.text: A little way repeated around the group of hills, which is most odd!

indicators.note: around says the doubled street abbreviation surrounds the hills

parts.note: ST, the abbreviation for street, given twice
a range is a line of hills or mountains

explanation.surface: A short road that loops twice round some hills: a very peculiar layout.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest is the superlative of strange, the most unusual or peculiar.

clue.text: Frightened? That's about right! (Though showing the results of a wound.)

definitions.text: showing the results of a wound

indicators.note: about says the word for frightened wraps round the abbreviation

parts.note: scared means frightened

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are frightened and agrees, though they bear the marks of injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred skin carries scars, the lasting marks left after a wound heals.

clue.text: A supporter of 14 with one who wants all eyes upon him proves to be one who found favor with Jehovah.

definitions.text: one who found favor with Jehovah

parts.note: the bra, the support for some ladies in the clue at 14 down

parts.words: one who wants all eyes upon him
parts.note: a ham is a showy performer who craves attention

explanation.surface: An attention-seeker wearing lingerie turns out to be favoured by God.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 14 down, whose wordplay used BRA for 'support for some ladies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham is the biblical patriarch God chose and blessed in the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: Seem wrong when the end is misplaced about it–with possession of land as one's own.

definitions.text: possession of land as one's own

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of seem are out of order
misplaced says the letters of end are out of place too

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something looks amiss when the end of a land deed is mislaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' and 'misplaced' together tell you to shuffle SEEM and END as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, demesne is holding land as one's own property, not as a tenant.

clue.text: Suburbanite who runs back and forth, but one possibly stumbles.

definitions.text: Suburbanite who runs back and forth
definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone making regular trips, as a commuter does
second meaning: one who trips over

explanation.walkthrough: The commuter and the clumsy person are two senses of one word built on 'trip'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is someone on a trip, a traveller, and also anyone who trips and falls.

clue.text: Pulls two strings together, and gets hooked, as they say.

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal
second meaning: the idiom for getting married, which slang also calls getting hitched or hooked

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights, 22 and 3 down. Both halves of the clue describe the same phrase, one literally, one as the idiom for a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie the knot is the everyday idiom for marrying, the same event slang calls getting hooked.

clue.text: Give all the elements, yet get nothing with the sign of victory, in what is said to come before fall.

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the proverb's word

parts.words: what is said to come before fall
parts.note: the proverb says pride comes before a fall
O is the shape of zero, nothing
V is the victory sign

explanation.surface: Supplying everything, yet ending with nothing but a victory salute before a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide is to supply what is needed, so giving every component.

clue.text: It's the wrong road for a girl who is so often called dumb.

definitions.text: a girl who is so often called dumb

indicators.note: the wrong road is the word with its letters disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl who took the wrong road gets called foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges ROAD. 'Dumb Dora' was American slang for a scatterbrained woman, from a 1920s comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dora is the girl's name fixed to the slang phrase for a silly woman.

clue.text: Avoids getting "quackers"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dodges
second meaning: birds that quack

explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks flag 'quackers' as a made-up name for the birds, not crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to evade, and the birds that quack are ducks, so one plural covers both.

clue.text: In alarum, be roused to find this may be raw or burnt.

definitions.text: this may be raw or burnt

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across alarum and be and roused

explanation.surface: A call to wake at the alarm, then find something left raw or overcooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'alarum, be roused'; alarum is an old word for alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earth pigment sold in two forms, raw umber and burnt umber, used by painters.

clue.text: Not up at the bottom of 24, say.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opposite direction to up
second meaning: the soft under-feathers of ducks

explanation.walkthrough: 24 refers to 24 down, DUCKS; their fine layer of feathers lies under the outer ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is both a direction opposite to up and the fluffy plumage beneath a bird's outer feathers.

clue.text: What boasters do, getting the bird.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to brag or gloat
second meaning: the black bird of the genus Corvus

explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, and the crow is also a common black bird.

clue.text: Don't stop! That's no good, and will get you a loud noisemaker!

parts.note: go is the opposite of stop

explanation.surface: A cry to keep going, then a complaint that it is no good and too noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gong is a large metal disc struck to make a loud resonant sound.

clue.text: Poetic gleamers–ten of them being in the Roman legion.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in Byron's poem The Destruction of Sennacherib the Assyrian's troops were 'gleaming in purple and gold'

definitions.text: ten of them being in the Roman legion
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a Roman legion was divided into ten tactical units of this kind

explanation.walkthrough: Byron's line runs 'And his cohorts were gleaming in purple and gold', so the poem supplies the gleamers; the legion supplies the plain sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was one tenth of a Roman legion, and Byron's famous couplet pictures such troops glittering.

clue.text: Play false with the lover more than once?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be unfaithful to a partner
second meaning, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: twice is more than once.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating on a partner by secretly seeing another is the slang sense; read literally the phrase means twice.

clue.text: The exact spot is not indicated, therefore I objectively have a point at this location.

definitions.text: The exact spot is not indicated

parts.note: so means therefore
me is the object form of I
W, west, is a compass point
here means at this place

explanation.surface: A vague location note: no exact spot given, so I have a point here.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere means in some place not specified, an unnamed location.

clue.text: One invited to your house might wax poetic.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a visitor you have invited
second meaning: Edgar ..., a popular American poet

explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Guest was a widely read American newspaper poet of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a person invited to visit, and Guest is also the surname of a well-known versifier.
